paragraphs.text: Split-hand/foot malformation-6 (SHFM6) is an autosomal recessive form of split-hand/foot malformation. It is marked by central reductions of the feet, with or without hand involvement, and the malformation pattern can vary within a family. Sporadic SHFM may be caused by this recessive form, which has implications for recurrence risk.

checks.evidence_quote: We studied a large consanguineous kindred afflicted with autosomal recessive SHFM.

checks.claim: SHFM6 is characterized by central reductions of the feet, with or without hand involvement.
checks.evidence_quote: Twelve affected members had central feet reductions with or without hand involvement

checks.claim: The SHFM6 malformation pattern can vary within a family.
checks.evidence_quote: A variable intrafamilial expression of the malformation pattern is apparent.
checks.explanation: The abstract directly reports variable expression within the family.

checks.claim: Sporadic split-hand/foot malformation may be caused by the recessive SHFM6 form, which has implications for recurrence risk.
checks.evidence_quote: Obviously, sporadic SHFM may show recessive rather than dominant inheritance resulting in a 25% recurrence risk for sibs instead of a very low-recurrence risk as generally presumed.

paragraphs.text: Ugur and Tolun (2008) used a candidate gene approach in a large consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM mapping to 12q13. They identified a homozygous missense mutation in the WNT10B gene (R332W). paragraphs.text: Kantaputra et al. (2018) identified a novel homozygous 3-bp deletion in the WNT10B gene (c.695_697delACA) in an Indian girl with SHFM6.
